objective: Earn a paid Plesk technical contribution by pitching an original reverse-SSH security guide grounded in current LazyTunnel and LazyEdge work, without writing a full unpaid article or treating submission as revenue.

source_need.title: Plesk Contributor Program
source_need.published_compensation: The landing page advertises USD 150-300 per accepted contribution; the linked submission guide states EUR 150-300 for a standard uncredited blog post and EUR 50 when author attribution is requested.
source_need.published_process: Submit a 150-250 word abstract, then wait up to three weeks. Successful applicants receive a contributor contract covering timeline, exclusivity, attribution, and pricing before writing.
source_need.payment_route: The linked guide states PayPal payments are processed on the 15th and 30th of each month.
source_need.policy: The currency discrepancy must be resolved by the written contract. Acceptance, a stated fee, publication, and payment are separate evidence states; the advertised range is not revenue.

fit.proposed_title: Keep Remote Administration Private with Reverse SSH and Loopback Listeners
supported_now: Current public OpenSSH, systemd, reverse-tunnel, loopback-listener, host-key-pinning, and rollback documentation
A public LazyRemote release with native management clients and an independent open-source tunnel core
A live seven-device deployment whose public README records 49 directed SSH checks
Existing LazyingArt technical articles and reproducible Linux examples
not_proven: Compatibility with every hosting provider or customer topology
A reboot test for every supported operating system
That an outbound SSH connection is permitted by every local network policy
Acceptance, publication, audience engagement, or payment from Plesk
fit.claim_boundary: The pitch proposes a standard-tool two-host lab and explicit negative checks. It does not offer firewall evasion, public desktop exposure, or a universal remote-access guarantee.

application.delivery_evidence: The complete form passed native validity checks, Submit was clicked once, and the embedded form returned its own contact confirmation message.

email_confirmation.terminal_evidence: The visible WebPros page confirmed that the email preferences were updated.
email_confirmation.policy: This completes the address-confirmation step requested after the contributor form. It may also update the sender's contact preference; it is not an editorial reply, proposal acceptance, contract, publication, payment, or revenue.

application.contract_gate: Do not draft the full article until a written contract states a fee of at least EUR 250 or equivalent, currency, PayPal eligibility, timeline, exclusivity, rights, revision boundary, attribution state, and payment trigger.
application.policy: The abstract and confirmation are an outbound proposal only. A successful response still requires a separate contract review before article work.
